newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish pound steady as market settles down.
newsitem.headline: Irish pound steady as market settles down.

text.p: The Irish pound held broadly steady against sterling and hovered around 2.58 marks in morning trade on Friday but dealers said trade was light and much of the recent volatility had gone out of the market.
"We are seeing consistent interest to buy Irish at 2.57 and to sell it at 2.60 against the mark and that is really tightening the volatility up," one dealer said.
But he said the outlook for the Irish pound against sterling remained uncertain and dealers would closely follow developments in sterling/mark in coming days.

"Everyone is focusing now on whether sterling has broken out of its uptrend. If it can hold above 2.75 marks, a very big level, we are still in an uptrend but if it tries to break below that, you could well see a big move in sterling."
A drop in sterling would be the best of all worlds for the Irish pound, allowing it to edge down against the mark and move up against sterling, alleviating inflationary fears, analysts said.
By 0952 GMT, the Irish pound was at 0.9330 sterling and $1.5150 against 0.9312 and $1.5103 at Thursday's close.
It was quoted at 2.5800 marks against 2.5788 last night.
Traders said a combination of a quieter tone in the currency market and soft inflation numbers yesterday had eased pressure on money market rates.
Ireland's April consumer price index rose by just 0.1 percent on the month.
On the interbank market, one-month money was quoted at 6.00/6.13 by 0944 GMT against 6.06/6.19 late on Thursday.
